name: Peppermint Crisp tart
summary: A no-bake fridge tart of coconut tea biscuits layered with whipped caramel cream and finished with a thick scattering of grated mint-crisp chocolate.
about: This fridge tart is one of South Africa's most-loved desserts. It is built from pantry staples: tinned caramel, coconut tea biscuits, fresh cream and the mint-crisp chocolate bar it is named after. It turns up at braais, birthdays and Christmas, and it needs no oven, just a night in the fridge for the biscuits to soften.

ingredients.name: Mint-crisp chocolate bars
ingredients.note: about 3 bars, grated or finely chopped

steps: Whip the cream in a large bowl with an electric beater on medium-high speed for 2–3 minutes, until it holds soft peaks that just flop over at the tips.

Spoon the caramel into a second bowl and beat for 1 minute until smooth and loose. Fold in a third of the whipped cream to lighten it, then gently fold in the rest until no streaks remain. Fold in a third of the grated chocolate.
Cover the base of a 20 x 30 cm glass or ceramic dish with a single layer of biscuits, breaking some to fill the gaps.
Spread half the caramel cream evenly over the biscuits. Add a second layer of biscuits, then spread the rest of the caramel cream over the top, smoothing it right to the edges.
Scatter the remaining grated chocolate thickly over the top. Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, preferably overnight, until the biscuits have softened enough to cut cleanly with a spoon.
Cut into 12 squares and serve straight from the fridge.
prepNote: Make it the day before; it keeps 3 days covered in the fridge.
